moves: Overseas pace is the most expensive market.

Established quicks enter at a ₹2 cr base, but in the 2026 mini-auction Pathirana went for ₹18 cr from that base. With four teams holding ₹39-47 cr and all short of pace, good overseas quicks should clear ₹7-8 cr.
Buy one premium overseas quick, not two.
Coetzee is the pick (max ₹8.5 cr). If he goes past that, RR moves down the pace ladder: Henry (₹7.5 cr), then Boult (₹6 cr). Two ₹7-8 cr quicks plus Wadhera would leave under ₹5 cr for three slots.
Indian middle-order batting is the second big spend.
Wadhera cost PBKS ₹4.2 cr; DC, KKR, MI and PBKS all need Indian batters, so expect ₹6-8 cr. His ceiling is ₹8 cr.
Fill the rest with value and youth.

Daryl Mitchell (unsold at ₹2 cr last year), Lomror (uncapped) and Karan Lal (unsold at ₹30 L in 2026, 20-ball fifty at RR trials) cost about ₹4-6 cr together. Rich teams spend early on stars; uncapped and young sets come later, when their purses are thinner.

The sixth buy is decided by price on the day: Deepak Chahar (Indian new ball, max ₹4.5 cr), Mitchell Owen (power hitter, max ₹3.5 cr) or Zak Foulkes (young pace all-rounder, max ₹1.5 cr). About ₹4.5 cr is held back for it.
Pathirana (₹10-16 cr) and Ferguson (₹8-12 cr) would take half the purse. RR lets them go; every crore rivals spend there is a crore less against RR later.

Targets total ₹20.5 cr of ₹27.05 cr. The ceilings are not all spent at once: any overspend on an early buy comes off the ceilings of later ones, so RR can always fill all 6 slots (minimum ₹30 L each).

brief_map: A data-learned Pressure Index (win-probability leverage × scoreboard squeeze × wicket squeeze). The top 25% of balls carry 55% of all win-probability movement.
Runs and wickets judged against an expected value for the exact match situation, adjusted for opposition strength and recency.
Empirical-Bayes shrinkage, 300 match bootstrap re-samples, split-half test and 9 alternative definitions.
One selection rule (buyable, active, 60+ pressure balls, IPL-tested), then ranked purely by NeRRve: rank 1 = highest-rated.
RR phase-by-phase pressure ranks set the gaps; every pick is mapped to a role and a slot in the XI.
Six core buys with target and walk-away prices, rival-purse analysis and a reserve.
Young talent watchlist from domestic and U19 cricket, kept separate from the ranked lists.
A dashboard with leaderboard weight sliders, player deep-dives, a pressure calculator and an auction basket.
